title: Giving few-shot examples to pin down output structure and style

videos.script: A prompt that works once is a demonstration. A prompt that works on the fortieth message, and the four hundredth, is a product. This course is about the distance between the two. {{title}} You will spend it with one prompt and a real model, running on your own computer. The prompt sorts the messages a small online bookshop receives, and answers in JSON: a category, an urgency and a one-line summary. {{triage}} The first thing you do is build the lab: Ollama, a small open model, and a harness of about two hundred lines that you can read. {{lab}} Then you count. Forty messages, five checks, and a number at the bottom. {{check}} The bare prompt passes none of them. Asking for JSON gets twenty-two. Three examples of the answer get twenty-eight, and the harness tells you how far to trust that jump. {{counts}} Then you break it on purpose. One order number left in one example, and the model hands it to customers who never mentioned it. {{leak}} By the end of the lesson you can tell what an example fixes and what it teaches by accident. And you can tell the two apart with a number. {{close}}
